# weather_client: instructions for coding agents

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

This is the generated Ruby client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request). The names below are exact: do not guess other package, import or method names.

- Install: `gem install weather_client -v 0.0.0`. The package is `weather_client` at version `0.0.0`.
- Import: `require 'weather_client'`.
- Client: `Weather::WeatherClient`. Construct it as below. `token:` in `Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig` is the bearer token's source: a callable returning the token (or nil to send none), called on every attempt so a refreshed token is used. `endpoint:` is the service's base URL.

```ruby
require 'weather_client'

client = Weather::WeatherClient.new(Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig.new(endpoint: ENV.fetch('WEATHER_ENDPOINT'), token: -> { ENV.fetch('WEATHER_TOKEN') }))
```

- Headers: The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request. Do not set them yourself.
- Operations: one method per operation, such as `create_city`, `get_city`, `get_city_photo`. Each takes its input type and returns its output type.
- Pagination: A paginated operation also has a `<operation>_pages` method returning an `Enumerator` of pages (`client.list_cities_pages(input).each do |page| ... end`): each page is one response, fetched as the enumerator is consumed, and it stops when the response carries no next token.
- Errors: Each modelled error is a class under `Weather`, a subclass of `Weather::WeatherException`: `rescue` it and read its members and `metadata.status` (a modelled `message` member is `message_value`). An error response the model does not describe raises `Weather::WeatherException` itself; no response raises `Weather::Runtime::NetworkError`, and a call outlasting `timeout:` raises `Weather::Runtime::DeadlineError`.
- Retries: automatic for safe calls; do not wrap calls in your own retry loop. Set `max_attempts:` in `Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), and `base_delay:` and `max_delay:` for the backoff.
- Idempotency: these calls fill an idempotency token when it is unset: `create_city` (`client_token`). Set it yourself to replay one logical request.
- Generated code: do not edit files in this package; they are replaced when it is regenerated.

## A complete call: `GetCity`

```ruby
require 'weather_client'

# The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
client = Weather::WeatherClient.new(Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig.new(endpoint: ENV.fetch('WEATHER_ENDPOINT'), token: -> { ENV.fetch('WEATHER_TOKEN') }))

# Values from the model's example "Read a city".
input = Weather::GetCityInput.new(
  city_id: 'c-0a1b2c3d',
  at: Weather::Runtime::Timestamp.parse('2026-01-02T03:04:05Z'),
)

begin
  output = client.get_city(input)
  p output.city
  p output.forecast
  p output.request_id
rescue Weather::NotFoundError => error
  warn "NotFoundError (HTTP #{error.metadata.status}): #{error.message_value}"
end
```

# weather_client

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

The Ruby client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request), generated by [Crucible](https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible) from the service's model.

## Install

```sh
gem install weather_client -v 0.0.0
```

The package is `weather_client`, version `0.0.0`; code refers to it as `weather_client`.

## Create a client

```ruby
require 'weather_client'

client = Weather::WeatherClient.new(Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig.new(endpoint: ENV.fetch('WEATHER_ENDPOINT'), token: -> { ENV.fetch('WEATHER_TOKEN') }))
```

`token:` in `Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig` is the bearer token's source: a callable returning the token (or nil to send none), called on every attempt so a refreshed token is used. `endpoint:` is the service's base URL. The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request.

## Call an operation

`get_city` calls `GetCity`. Every operation has a method like it.

```ruby
require 'weather_client'

# The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
client = Weather::WeatherClient.new(Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig.new(endpoint: ENV.fetch('WEATHER_ENDPOINT'), token: -> { ENV.fetch('WEATHER_TOKEN') }))

# Values from the model's example "Read a city".
input = Weather::GetCityInput.new(
  city_id: 'c-0a1b2c3d',
  at: Weather::Runtime::Timestamp.parse('2026-01-02T03:04:05Z'),
)

begin
  output = client.get_city(input)
  p output.city
  p output.forecast
  p output.request_id
rescue Weather::NotFoundError => error
  warn "NotFoundError (HTTP #{error.metadata.status}): #{error.message_value}"
end
```

## Pagination

A paginated operation also has a `<operation>_pages` method returning an `Enumerator` of pages (`client.list_cities_pages(input).each do |page| ... end`): each page is one response, fetched as the enumerator is consumed, and it stops when the response carries no next token.

```ruby
require 'weather_client'

# The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
client = Weather::WeatherClient.new(Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig.new(endpoint: ENV.fetch('WEATHER_ENDPOINT'), token: -> { ENV.fetch('WEATHER_TOKEN') }))

# Values from the model's example "List the first page".
input = Weather::ListCitiesInput.new(
  max_results: 2,
  tags: [
    'coastal',
    'capital',
  ],
)

# Each page is one response; the paginator sends `next_token` for the next.
client.list_cities_pages(input).each do |page|
  p page.cities
end
```

## Errors

Each modelled error is a class under `Weather`, a subclass of `Weather::WeatherException`: `rescue` it and read its members and `metadata.status` (a modelled `message` member is `message_value`). An error response the model does not describe raises `Weather::WeatherException` itself; no response raises `Weather::Runtime::NetworkError`, and a call outlasting `timeout:` raises `Weather::Runtime::DeadlineError`.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. An idempotency token the caller leaves unset is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: `create_city` (`client_token`). Set `max_attempts:` in `Weather::Runtime::ClientConfig` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), and `base_delay:` and `max_delay:` for the backoff.

## Links

- [Home](<https://weather.example/docs>)
- [The Ruby client guide](<https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible/blob/main/docs/clients/ruby.md>)

=== lib/weather_client/models/location.rb ===
# frozen_string_literal: true
module Weather
    class Location
      def self.from_wire(value, context)
        object = ::Weather::Runtime::WireCodec.object(value)
        raise ::ArgumentError, 'Union requires one member' unless object.size == 1
        key, value = object.first
        case key
        when 'coordinates' then CoordinatesVariant.new(value.nil? ? nil : context.codec.decode(value, context.member(key)))
        when 'unknown' then UnknownVariant.new(value.nil? ? nil : context.codec.decode(value, context.member(key)))
        else Unknown.new(key, ::Weather::Runtime::JsonValue.new(value))
        end
      end
      class CoordinatesVariant < Location
        # @return [Coordinates, nil] the member's value; nil when the union carries an explicit null
        attr_reader :value
        def initialize(value)
          @value = value
          freeze
        end
        def to_wire(context)
          {'coordinates' => @value.nil? ? nil : context.codec.encode(@value, context.member('coordinates'))}
        end
        def inspect = Runtime::Describe.format('Location', {coordinates: @value})
        alias to_s inspect
      end
      class UnknownVariant < Location
        # @return [Runtime::Unit, nil] the member's value; nil when the union carries an explicit null
        attr_reader :value
        def initialize(value)
          @value = value
          freeze
        end
        def to_wire(context)
          {'unknown' => @value.nil? ? nil : context.codec.encode(@value, context.member('unknown'))}
        end
        def inspect = Runtime::Describe.format('Location', {unknown: @value})
        alias to_s inspect
      end
      # A member this client does not know, kept so it can be sent back unchanged.
      class Unknown < Location
        # @return [String] the member name received
        attr_reader :name
        # @return [Runtime::JsonValue] the raw value received
        attr_reader :value
        # Omits the value: nothing says whether it is sensitive.
        def inspect = Runtime::Describe.format('Location', {unknown_variant: @name})
        alias to_s inspect
        def initialize(name, value)
          @name = ::Weather::Runtime::WireCodec.string(name).freeze
          raise ::ArgumentError, 'Expected JsonValue' unless value.is_a?(::Weather::Runtime::JsonValue)
          @value = value
          freeze
        end
        def to_wire(context)
          raise ::ArgumentError, 'Unknown variant name is declared' if context.shape.fetch('members').key?(@name)
          {@name => @value.value}
        end
      end
    end
end
